subject: Post-demo: integration constraints + model routing and policy follow-ups
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.com>, Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: integration constraints + model routing and policy follow-ups

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation. I wanted to capture the key takeaways and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned.

Recap (short):
- Goal: replace current ML API for search + rerank with Redwood-hosted endpoints, plus on-prem/private deployment for regulated workloads.
- Primary workloads: interactive chat (low latency, <=200ms target for tail), semantic search + reranking (batched embeddings + rerankers), occasional long-generation jobs.

Open technical items (from our side to confirm):
1) SDK / auth: you mentioned a preference for client SDKs (Node + Java) and using your existing IAM. We recommend Redwood SDK v1.4.0 (supports mTLS + API-key fallback). We'll outline auth options (API key, OAuth service account with short-lived tokens, and mutual TLS for Private).
2) Network: need VPC peering / egress rules for Private deployment; SecOps asked about IP allowlists and audit logs.
3) Model routing & policies: we discussed latency vs cost policy — e.g., route latency-sensitive requests to low-latency region + smaller but faster model, with fallback to higher-quality model on Dedicated capacity if quality thresholds are missed. We should capture your SLOs (p50/p95), expected qps, and cost targets.
4) Structured output & tools: you want tool-calling for DB lookups and deterministic JSON outputs for UI rendering. We'll propose a schema-based structured-output config and example tool adapters.
5) Embeddings & reranking: confirm embedding vector size and index (approx %) so we can size dedicated indexing nodes and suggest quantization.

Attachments: Redwood integration guide (attached) — includes SDK quickstart, sample model-routing policies, and auth patterns.

Next steps:
- Dev deep-dive: schedule a 60-90min architecture session with your platform + SecOps to walk through network/auth/fallback chains (Dev recommended attendees).
- Provide: expected qps, latency SLOs, sample payload sizes, and a copy of your network diagram.
- We'll prepare a draft model-routing policy and cost/latency tradeoff table ahead of the deep-dive.

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Thu 3/12 10am-12pm PST or Fri 3/13 9am-11am PST.

Thanks — looping in Dev and Lauren to drive the tech discussion.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | (415) 555-0193
redwood.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Post-demo: integration constraints + model routing and policy follow-ups

Hi Sanjay / Lisa — following up with technical details and a short primer we can use in the architecture deep-dive.

1) SDK & Auth notes
- Recommended: Redwood SDK v1.4.0 (NodeJS, Java). Includes built-in retry/backoff, streaming client, and structured-output helpers. Quickstart is in the attached guide.
- Auth options:
  * API key (short-lived, scoped per-route) — easiest for early POC.
  * OAuth service account + short-lived tokens (recommended for automation).
  * mTLS + client certs (for Private deployment / air-gapped).
- We can integrate with your existing identity provider (Okta). We support OIDC service accounts and can issue scoped tokens.

2) Model routing + policy configuration (high level)
- Policy primitives: latency_threshold_ms, cost_budget_per_1k_tokens, quality_threshold (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE or RL-based score), region_preference, capacity_tier (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Example routing strategy (pseudo):
  * If latency_required <= 200ms AND region == us-west -> route -> fast-variant (gptx-small-ll) on hosted pool
  * Else if quality_score < threshold -> fallback to gptx-medium-ll on Dedicated (higher cost)
  * If region == eu -> route to eu-optimized model pool
- We will provide a JSON policy you can drop into the Console; during the deep-dive we can tune rules based on your p95 target and cost constraints.

3) Embeddings & reranking
- Need: vector dimension (128/256/768), average number of candidate docs per query, expected write QPS for indexing.
- Options: offline indexing (batch embeddings) or streaming (real-time updates). For high-QPS search + rerank, we recommend approximate NN index with quantization (OPQ + 8-bit) to reduce memory.

4) Structured output & tool-calling
- We support function/tool calling and schema-based structured outputs (strict JSON schema enforcement).
- For deterministic UI rendering, we can enforce response schemas and failover to a canonical parser when outputs deviate.

Please reply with the following so we can size and plan before the session:
- target p50/p95 latency, expected qps (peak & avg), avg token length for queries/responses, preferred region(s), and whether Private/VPC is required for the POC.

Happy to present the routing policy examples in the deep-dive.

— Dev
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

Attachment: (referenced in Marcus' note) redwood-integration-guide.pdf

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: integration constraints + model routing and policy follow-ups

Thanks Marcus & Dev — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications before the deep-dive:

1) Fallback chains: when you say fallback to Dedicated for quality, does that require request-level failover (synchronous) or async re-score? Our UI expects synchronous responses for search.
2) Cost vs latency: interested in a worked example showing the incremental cost of moving from small->medium models at our expected QPS; can you include estimates?
3) Region routing: we operate primarily in us-west and eu-west. For latency-sensitive queries from eu users, we'd rather route to eu-hosted variants. How does cross-region failover impact consistency of rerankers and embeddings?

A couple of requests:
- We're available for the deep-dive Fri 3/13 10am-11:30am PST.
- Attached our internal network diagram and a short SecOps checklist (acme-network-diagram.pdf).

Sending the initial answers to your sizing questions:
- peak qps (search queries): 120 qps (expected peak during business hours), avg qps: 30
- desired p50/p95 latency: <=100ms / <=250ms for search path (including rerank)
- avg tokens: query 24 tokens, response 120 tokens
- embeddings: 768-dim, ~20M docs initially, mostly read-heavy (few indexing writes per minute)
- POC mode: hosted Dedicated (not on-prem) but must meet data isolation requirements and audit logs.

Let us know if you need anything else ahead of the call.

— Sanjay
Senior Product Manager | ACME Corp
Attachments: acme-network-diagram.pdf (2.1MB)
